1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes or high values.  
2. Model underestimates prices during periods of strong upward momentum, particularly when true values rise sharply after a dip.  
3. Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price declines — forecasts remain high while prices fall.  
4. Model tends to overshoot after sharp price increases, then fails to correct downward quickly.  
5. Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price behavior suggests.  
6. Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent low values, leading to premature pessimism when prices rebound.  
7. Model fails to capture the “tail” of price spikes — often underestimates the magnitude of late-period surges.  
8. Forecast smoothing is too aggressive — fails to reflect sudden, volatile shifts in price direction.
